analysis.title: #GLOBALMARKETS WEEKLY WRAP-UP, October 10, 2026
key_insights: Money market funds took in $166.4B in the week to Oct 7 (BofA/EPFR), the largest weekly inflow since April 2020. Assets reached $8T, up from $5T in 2023, and the inflow more than reversed the prior week's $118B quarter-end outflow.

The S&P 500 rose 1.15% on the week, the Dow +0.93%, the Nasdaq Composite +0.64%, and the Russell 2000 fell. Consumer staples, utilities and energy led, while industrials and information technology declined.
The S&P 500 closed at a record 7,819 on Tuesday, its 28th record of the year. Goldman's Shawn Tuteja noted the index is up 1.3% since Aug 27 while the S&P excluding AI names is down 5.2%.

Breadth is poor beneath the record index. Sept 7 data cited: 15 straight days of more new lows than new highs on the S&P 500. Nomura's McElligott counts 85% of constituents more than 10% below their highs and 59% more than 20% below, which he calls a 'rolling correction'.

YTD the S&P 500 is +15.2%, the equal-weight S&P 500 +12% and the S&P 500 ex-AI +7%. Since the mid-Sept low, two-thirds of index stocks have fallen further. The equal-weight index remains more than 5% below its peak.
Since Aug 3, the Mag7 is up 7.7%, the S&P 500 up 2.6% and the equal-weight S&P 500 down 3%.

Only about 23% of the largest 500 US stocks have beaten the S&P 500 over 10 years (about 22% across the largest 2,000), the lowest in at least two decades. Both shares have more than halved in a decade and were above 50% after the global financial crisis.
The RSP/SPY ratio (equal-weight vs cap-weight S&P 500) hit a new all-time low, and the tech-to-S&P 500 ratio has never been higher.
The market is piling into the quality factor (low-debt balance sheets) and dumping the most-shorted stocks.
The Mag7 ETF (MAGS) had its largest monthly inflow ever in September at $1.04B, taking cumulative flows to a record $4.34B.
Nvidia hit a new all-time high of $243 on Wednesday.

Goldman expects a strong Q3 earnings season. S&P 500 EPS growth is expected at 27% driven by AI, versus 9% for the median stock (down from 14% in Q2). AI infrastructure stocks drive over half of EPS growth, the top 10 stocks over two-thirds, and Micron plus Nvidia more than one-third.

Samsung guided Q3 revenue +127% and operating profit +783%, but shares fell about 2.5% because the profit reflects memory shortages and prices that can reverse. TSMC September revenue was +54.6%, taking Q3 revenue growth to roughly 51%.
Micron net income is up 42x in two years to $38B, $8B more than Apple earned last quarter, which the source reads as pricing power in a memory shortage.

FT reported OpenAI told investors annualized revenue was approaching $50B at the end of September, about $20B below the $68-70B figure that circulated weeks earlier. OpenAI's tokenized price fell and did not rebound on Friday.
Reported cuts to internal Claude use at Microsoft (per-employee budgets from $100K to $10K a month) and Meta suggest companies are treating AI tokens as a real budget.

The 10-year Treasury yield reached about 5.36% intraday on Wednesday and Thursday, the highest since 2002, with the 30-year above 5.70%. Both finished the week roughly unchanged after stronger-than-expected auctions. 2s30s topped 90bp, the widest since mid-August, before flattening back.

Fed minutes: all 19 officials backed a 25bp hike in September, and most said another increase would likely be appropriate by year-end. December hike odds are about 80%, with an October skip seen at roughly one in five.

Credit shows stress that equities do not: Oracle 5-year CDS hit a record 261bp and Broadcom's a record 136bp. CCC spreads are at 1,014bp (three-year wide, +224bp in three months) while IG sits near 59bp and the VIX is 15.4, in the 17th percentile of its one-year range.

SpaceX's BBB-rated 2056 bonds trade around 85 cents on the dollar with spreads like junk debt. SpaceX also agreed to buy nationwide 800 MHz spectrum from Grain Management, and AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile fell in extended trading.

French 10-year spreads over Bunds reached nearly 160bp last Friday, the widest since 2011, then tightened to about 140bp after Le Pen's counter-budget. The OAT was back near 4.90% Thursday after the government's 2027 budget targeted a 5% deficit and a record €340B borrowing requirement. France's 10-year (4.79%) yields more than Greece's (4.43%).

Oil: Brent topped $105-106 intraday Thursday and WTI above $93 before retreating after Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterms. Hormuz flows are about 9.5 mb/d, roughly 30% below pre-war. Dated Brent surged near post-war highs, and a Gulf-to-Far East supertanker costs about $1.3M a day versus under $50K before the war. Persian Gulf exports including dark flows are back to 23.3 mb/d, about 93% of the 2025 average.

US diesel is near $6.32 a gallon. Trump is temporarily allowing red diesel on public roads and deferring a 24-cent federal tax through year-end. A diesel export ban was dropped after European allies agreed to release stockpiles.
Houthis launched a large missile and drone attack on Saudi Arabia, including Riyadh airport and an Aramco facility, raising Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb shipping risk.

The dollar index touched its highest since April 2025. EURUSD hit 1.1160 Monday, a 17-month low. Gold finished the week higher after rebounding Friday. Copper closed Thursday +2.1% at $6.735/lb. The Brazilian real gained over 4% through 5.00 per dollar, its best week since July 2022.

The Ibovespa rose 7.7% on one day to a record 206,912 and about 9% on the week. EWZ had its highest notional day in its 25-year history at $8B on Monday. Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro an 84% chance in the Oct 25 runoff against Lula (first-round polling 47% vs 45%).

Bitcoin fell from about $87,000 Tuesday to almost $80,000 Thursday, then bounced Friday and found support at its 50-day moving average. Spot ETF outflows were sizable in the last couple of days, and bitcoin traded like the highest-beta part of the Nasdaq during a week of fiscal alarm.
Truflation's daily US CPI is 2.92% y/y and rising, its high for the year, but below the BLS reported rate of 3.40%. The UN food price index rose to 136 in September, the highest since Nov 2022.

Net income is up 42x in two years to $38B, which the source cites as evidence of pricing power in a memory shortage.
Samsung's Q3 guidance showed revenue +127% and operating profit +783%, yet the shares fell about 2.5% because memory-price-driven profit can reverse quickly.
5-year CDS hit a record 261bp after a revenue question was raised about its largest customer.
5-year CDS hit a record 136bp on the same customer revenue question.
Fell in extended trading after SpaceX agreed to buy nationwide 800 MHz spectrum, a step toward competing directly with carriers.

Energy led the week as Brent topped $105 and Hormuz flows stayed about 30% below pre-war levels.
Both led weekly performance, consistent with money moving into defensive and quality exposures.
Industrials were among the week's biggest decliners.

TSMC reported September revenue +54.6% and Q3 revenue growth of roughly 51%.

risk_factors: Narrow equity breadth: index records are driven by AI names while most stocks are in a rolling correction.
Long-end yields at the highest since 2002 and a Fed in a tightening cycle with another hike likely by year-end.
Oil and Hormuz supply disruption, with shipping attacks and Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia.
AI revenue risk: OpenAI revenue reportedly about $20B below earlier circulated figures, and hyperscaler credit spreads at records for Oracle and Broadcom.
Memory pricing power can reverse quickly (Samsung's reaction).
French fiscal stress and sovereign spreads at the widest since 2011.
Weak Bitcoin price action and ETF outflows tied to liquidity conditions.
Inflation pressure from food, diesel and shipping costs.
